name: Respiratory variants & flu
summary: Early flu season driven by a drifted H1N1 strain in the US and UK
state: CDC said US flu hospitalisations in the week to 17 Oct were the highest for that week since 2010–11, with H1N1 carrying a G155E mutation making up 239 of 241 subtyped flu A samples. In England, flu positivity rose to 6.5% by 4 Oct and UKHSA flagged an H1N1 virus drifted from the vaccine strain (9 Oct).
for_you: Follow NHS and UKHSA advice; eligible groups can get the autumn flu vaccine.
rubric_hit: Unusually early flu season in the northern hemisphere = Watch

sources.title: Nature World News — Early H1N1 wave pushes mid-October flu hospitalisation rate to highest since 2010–11

why: Known viruses change; a new COVID-19 variant or a severe flu strain can strain health systems without being 'novel'.
drivers: Viral evolution, waning immunity, seasonal patterns, vaccine match.

rubric.alert: WHO designates a variant of concern, or flu or COVID-19 hospitalisations strain several countries' health systems.
rubric.watch: WHO designates a new variant of interest, or a hemisphere's flu season is unusually early or severe.
rubric.normal: No WHO variant of interest rising fast; flu seasons of normal severity.
